question:
Consider the system
$$x+y+z=3$$
$$2x+3y+4z=8$$
$$3x+4y+5z=k$$

(a) Show that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is zero.

(b) Determine the value of $k$ for which the system is consistent.

(c) For this value of $k$, state the number of solutions and express the solution in terms of one parameter.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\2 & 3 & 4\\3 & 4 & 5\end{bmatrix}$$
Since $R_3=R_1+R_2$, the rows are dependent. Therefore,
$$|A|=0$$

(b)
The left-hand side of the third equation is the sum of the left-hand sides of the first and second equations. For consistency, its right-hand side must also be their sum.
$$k=3+8=11$$
Thus, the system is consistent when $k=11$. If $k\neq11$, it is inconsistent.

(c)
For $k=11$, the third equation is dependent on the first two equations. Hence, the system has infinitely many solutions.
Let $z=t$. From the first equation,
$$x+y=3-t$$
Subtracting twice the first equation from the second equation gives
$$y+2z=2$$
Therefore,
$$y=2-2t$$
Then,
$$x=3-t-(2-2t)=1+t$$
Hence, the infinitely many solutions are
$$x=1+t,\quad y=2-2t,\quad z=t,\quad t\in\mathbb{R}$$

options.A:
(a) $|A|=1$
(b) $k=11$
(c) The system has the unique solution $(1,2,0)$
options.C:
(a) $|A|=0$
(b) $k=11$
(c) The system has the unique solution $(1,2,0)$
options.D:
(a) $|A|=0$ because $R_3=R_1+R_2$
(b) $k=11$
(c) Infinitely many solutions: $x=1+t,\ y=2-2t,\ z=t,\ t\in\mathbb{R}$
